title: Artificial Intelligence in Finance and the Early-Career Skills Shift: A Structured Evidence Synthesis of Decision Delegation, Bank Deployments, and Business Education
abstract: arXiv:2611.23261v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming a general interaction and decision-support layer across finance. Banks use AI for research retrieval, document synthesis, meeting follow-up, customer service, coding, fraud detection, risk support, and increasingly multi-step workflows. This paper asks which parts of finance work can be delegated safely, which remain human-owned, and how education should change when AI compresses the tasks through which novices traditionally build judgment. It presents a structured evidence synthesis of research and public evidence released from 2023 through October 2026 across finance, labor economics, education, bank deployments, and financial regulation. Numerical results and deployment claims remain attributed to their original sources. Four connections emerge: AI is strongest at retrieval, transformation, coding, and first-pass analysis; financial institutions are moving toward constrained rather than unrestricted

translated_title: 金融领域的人工智能与早期职业技能转变：关于决策委托、银行部署与商业教育的结构化证据综合
translated_abstract: 人工智能正在成为金融领域通用的交互与决策支持层。银行将AI用于研究检索、文档综合、会议跟进、客户服务、编程、欺诈检测、风险支持，以及日益增多的多步骤工作流程。本文探讨金融工作中哪些部分可以安全地委托给AI，哪些仍必须由人类主导，以及当AI压缩了新手传统上借以培养判断力的任务时，教育应当如何转变。本文对2023年至2026年10月间发布的金融、劳动经济学、教育、银行部署和金融监管等领域的研究成果与公开证据进行了结构化的证据综合，数值结果和部署声明均标注其原始来源。研究揭示了四项关键关联：AI在检索、转换、编程和初步分析方面表现最强；金融机构正朝着受限而非不受限的方向推进应用……
tldr: 本文通过结构化的证据综合，系统梳理了金融工作中哪些任务可安全委托给AI、哪些须保留人类主导，并指出在AI压缩新手历练路径的背景下商业教育亟需转型。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a structured evidence synthesis identifying which finance tasks can be safely delegated to AI versus kept human-owned, and how business education must adapt as AI compresses the tasks through which early-career professionals traditionally build judgment.
